Previous wind forecast improvement efforts have been conducted across the Midwest 3 and Central Plains (WFIP1: Wilczak et al. 2015) as well as the Columbia River Basin region in the U.S. Pacific Northwest (WFIP2: Shaw et al. 2019). WFIP3 is the first WFIP focused on the coastal oceanic environment, and involved numerous research institutions, including four DOE National Labs, three NOAA Research Labs, two NOAA Weather Forecasting Offices, and multiple universities and private companies. WFIP3 was carried out on the U.S. East Coast (Fig. 1) as it is both a high-use coastal zone and exhibits strong seasonality in atmospheric and oceanic properties at a range of scales (Sorooshian et al. 2020; Lentz 2008; Wang et al. 2018; Shutt and Seim 2020). In the region, seasonal and event scale variations in air and water temperatures, atmospheric stability, storm tracks, and oceanic mixed layer depths drive a dynamic coastal zone (e.g. Lombardo and Kading 2018). Low-level jets (LLJs), a key atmospheric boundary layer phenomena, are ubiquitous in the region, as demonstrated by prior studies (Archer et al. Fig. 1. The project focused on the Northeast shelf to take advantage of existing observational assets including numerous land-based instrumented sites proximate to the coastal zone and an offshore fixed tower. These assets allowed the project to address key research topics, including: the vertical structure of momentum 4 flux in atmospheric and oceanic surface layers; parameterizations of boundary layer clouds, moist convective and precipitation processes, and their linkages to changes in ocean surface conditions and coastal weather phenomena including squall lines, marine fog, cold-air outbreaks, and winter storms. Field observations were conducted primarily between November 2023 and August 2025, with mobilization and demobilization continuing into November of 2025. All analysis of project collected data was halted on October 2nd, 2025 as a result of the termination of the project by the Department of Energy via email at that time, which was later adjusted to October 9th, 2025. Recovery of field assets after the date of termination was approved by DOE to continue into the fall of 2025 as part of the terminated project close out activities. In the text that follows, we describe the project's focus, the scope of the field campaign, and the datasets available for future research studies.
